Lemma
[Finite-time singularity models are noncompact when $\lambda \le 0$] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0030 ↗ lem:chow-iii-ch17-volume-lower-nonpositive-lambda ↗ rem:chow-iii-ch17-singularity-models 1. ch17:17.10\group Finite Time Singularities

If a singular closed Ricci flow has $\lambda (g(t))\le 0$ throughout, every finite-time singularity model is noncompact.
Proof

\sketch For a blow-up factor $K_i\to \infty $, the rescaled time-zero volume is $K_i^{n/2}\Vol (g(t_i))$. The preceding volume lower bound makes this tend to infinity. Smooth convergence to a compact model would instead make it converge to that model’s finite volume, a contradiction.

□
